newsitem.title: USA: CBOT unveils new 60,000 square-foot trading floor.
newsitem.headline: CBOT unveils new 60,000 square-foot trading floor.

text.p: When the financial futures opening bell rang Tuesday morning, the Chicago Board of Trade became the world's biggest futures exchange in terms of square footage as well as volume, an exchange spokesman said.

The $182 million addition of 60,000 square feet gives the CBOT a total of 92,000 square feet of agricultural and financial trading, "the largest continuous trading hall in the world," a CBOT spokesman said.
The CBOT already leads the rest of the world in terms of exchange volume, with January's trading volume reported at 18,991,093 contracts, the exchange said.

The new facility is more than three times the size of the CBOT's former "bond room", which closed on Friday. The extra room will allow volume at the exchange to grow, said Pat Arbor, the exchange's chairman.
"I would think that we would see a modest increase in volume, maybe five to 10 percent," Arbor said in a recent interview. "That's what we're building it for," Arbor said.
This new trading hall, which took two years to build, is designed for a population of 8,000 and outfitted with 876 booths located around and among eight trading pits.
The exchange said the trading floor can accommodate up to 2,000 more booths, with room in the building for a whole new trading floor above, if necessary.

As the first day of trade in the new trading hall wore on, floor traders were busy acclimating themselves to the new environment -- finding new sightlines, working with new brokers and weathering minor technical glitches.
"It's a good thing it's pretty slow in here," one bond options trader said. "If it were busy it would show the cracks a little more."
A CBOT spokesman reported a minor problem with a price board, but said it was fixed immediately.
Overall, traders said they were pleased with their new home.
"We're getting acclimated to the floor, but things are pretty good and there's a lot of excitement," said Don Pullen, trading floor bond manager for ED and F Man.
